title: New UFO files reveal Pentagon's plan for secret underground vault to keep 'exotic' material
byline: Edited by Aryan Singh / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Nov 21, 2026, 19:09 IST
excerpt: What do a secret underground vault, unidentified objects spotted by fighter pilots and mysterious radar detections have in common?
content:
Pentagon unveiled a treasure trove of documents on UFO investigations dating as far back as the 1950s

What do a secret underground vault, unidentified objects spotted by fighter pilots and mysterious radar detections have in common?They all feature in a fresh batch of US government UFO files, offering a glimpse into decades of investigations into unexplained aerial phenomena.The Pentagon on Friday released 43 files, including a 538-page report by government contractor Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), which detailed plans for a heavily secured underground vault in Nevada to store potentially recovered "exotic material or tissue", biological samples and unidentified hardware.The documents also contain accounts of UFO sightings dating back to the 1950s, military encounters, historical intelligence assessments and recent radar detections that investigators have been unable to conclusively explain.According to a 538-page report dated July 2009, prepared by Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), the contractor had proposed constructing a highly secure underground facility at its premises in North Las Vegas, Nevada.The report outlined plans for a vault buried 15 to 20 feet underground, with a storage area spanning 5,000 square feet. The proposed facility was to have three-foot-thick walls, a heavy steel door and extensive camouflage to conceal any structures visible above ground.

The facility was intended to store potentially recovered "exotic material or tissue", biological samples and hardware that BAASS might obtain from private individuals, research groups and other sources, including Brazil.However, the document describes a proposed facility and anticipated acquisitions. It does not establish that BAASS had actually recovered extraterrestrial material or that the underground vault was ever built.Reported UFO sightings dating back to the 1950sThe newly released documents contain several accounts of unexplained aerial sightings reported by military personnel, fighter pilots and civilians across different countries.Some of the records date back to the 1950s, with witnesses describing unusual flying objects, mysterious lights and encounters that investigators could not conclusively identify.One of the notable accounts dates back to 1953 and involves Clarence "Kelly" Johnson, the legendary Lockheed engineer who played a key role in developing the U-2 and SR-71 spy aircraft.According to an Air Force report, Johnson described seeing a dark, elliptical object hovering motionless against a sunset sky at his ranch in California. He said he observed the object through binoculars for around three minutes before it moved away in a shallow climb.The report also mentioned a Lockheed test crew flying offshore that reportedly saw a large, flying-wing-shaped object around the same time. However, an Air Force assessment later classified Johnson's sighting as a lenticular cloud.Another account in the files describes a reported encounter involving a US Air Force fighter pilot near Ube, Japan, in December 1956.According to an Air Force intelligence report dated December 17, the pilot, attached to the 68th Fighter-Interceptor Squadron, detected an unidentified radar return that remained visible for seven to eight minutes. He also reported seeing an object resembling the upper half of a sphere.The pilot estimated that the object was moving at a speed of 1,500 to 1,800 knots. However, neither ground radar nor the radar equipment of his wingman detected the object, leaving the encounter unexplained.The newly released records also cover more recent military encounters, including the 2004 USS Nimitz incident and a reported encounter involving US F-15C fighter pilots near Britain's RAF Lakenheath in 2007.

The latest release also includes three videos captured by US central command in 2020, 2023 and 2026, showing unidentified objects or areas of contrast recorded by military sensors.Despite the unusual accounts, the documents do not establish that any of the sightings involved extraterrestrial objects or technology.
